failures.criterion: Architect's ruling under the 'fix it here' rule (2026-10-26 10:07Z, envoy dcd100dd283040ed542b02e9a13c49b7). Once the session or interest bucket's stream is recreated, the copy stops reporting Following before it applies any record of the new stream, and the listener starts the full re-read without waiting for the self-health tick. From then on the normal rules hold: the copy keeps its records and serves them within the stale bound, and the re-read sweeps only once it completes. The adv-expiry scenarios (recreate 28 s before a tick, with the old stream shorter and longer than the new one) become a regression scenario in the rig (packages/envoy/scripts/e2e-refill.sh) that fails on b6d4733. Design is the implementer's choice: the JetStream stream deleted/created advisories, or treating an entry from a stream other than w.stream (or the ordered consumer's reset) as the end of following. A missed advisory must still be caught by the existing Check.
failures.evidence: At b6d4733, between a bucket recreate and the next self-health Check (up to 30 s), the old ordered consumer re-attaches to the new stream at the old stream's last sequence + 1. Following() stays true, the epoch does not move, and the new bucket's records in the skipped range never arrive. Real listener: $TMPDIR/infra261-test/adv-expiry-head shows GET /v1/sessions without 40 of the bucket's 2000 records from T-19.8 s until the tick's re-read completed at T+8 s. adv-expiry2-head (old stream longer) shows nothing of the new bucket before the tick. adv-expiry-base shows main 748e8d95 behaves the same before the tick. Red test, commit 2fa7c3d6081c: packages/envoy/internal/kvwatch/recreated_under_watch_test.go TestABucketRecreatedUnderALiveWatcherIsReadWholeWithoutCheck. `cd packages/envoy && go test ./internal/kvwatch/ -run TestABucketRecreatedUnderALiveWatcherIsReadWholeWithoutCheck -count=1 -v` fails at head. old_stream_shorter: '20s after the recreate: ghost kept true, 3 of 40 new records missing, Following true, Epoch 0 (37 new records applied)' and '37 records of the new bucket were applied while the copy still reported Following (first "fresh-03")'. old_stream_longer: '40 of 40 new records missing, Following true, Epoch 0 (0 new records applied)'. Apart from this, the spec's acceptance holds at b6d4733 (proof below).

proof.criterion: Acceptance 1, last clause: a session whose old record expires during the read, and whose heartbeat renewed it in the new bucket, is never left out
proof.surface: real listener + natsd. S was registered through the listener 298 s before the re-read (its record expires at T+2 s). Its renewal was written into the recreated bucket after 100000 markers. NATS was SIGSTOPped for 7 s at the read's start, so the expiry falls inside the read.
proof.observed: Every poll from T-21 s to T+7.3 s listed S with its old title 'refill hb 0 v1', across its T+2 s expiry, while the read was stalled. The read then delivered 201, 693 and 1296 rows, each with S, and completed at T+9.1 s with 2001 entries, S as 'refill hb 0 v2'.
proof.negativeControl: The 748e8d95 build in the same timeline answered 19 polls of 200 [] (S absent) from T+0.4 s, then partial lists without S, until its read completed at T+9.2 s.

proof.observed: Before: /v1/sessions 200 with 50 rows, gauges 50/50, /api/v1/agents 200 with 50 rows, issue route_status live with holder ses_refill_live_0, envoy_sessions listed 50. NATS down: every poll answered 200 until the first 503 at +121 s. Then /v1/sessions and /v1/interests/ answered 503 Retry-After: 5 {"code":"refilling"}, and /metrics had no envoy_active_* sample. /api/v1/agents answered 503 Retry-After: 5 ENVOY_REFILLING. Before the first read, with no NATS, both lists answered the refilling 503 with an empty gauge, and per-session reads answered 'service starting'.

testGaps.gap: No test covered the claim chip or the Unclaimed filter while the agent list refills (ClaimChip.test.tsx and issue-filters.test.ts gained only fixture lines).
